title: Article 61 — Procedure for impeachment of the President

content.overview: Article 61 provides the procedure for impeachment of the President for violation of the Constitution. A charge may be preferred by either House of Parliament. The resolution containing the proposal must be moved after at least fourteen days’ notice in writing signed by not less than one-fourth of the total number of members of the House, and must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House. The other House investigates (or causes investigation of) the charge; the President has the right to appear and be represented. If the investigating House sustains the charge by a resolution passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its total membership, the President is removed from office from the date of the resolution.
content.glance: Impeachment for violation of the Constitution. Either House prefers charge (1/4 notice; 2/3 of total membership). Other House investigates; 2/3 of total membership sustains → removal.
content.study:
Article 61 procedure:
1. Charge for violation of the Constitution may be preferred by either House.
2. Resolution: moved only after 14 days’ written notice signed by ≥1/4 of total membership of that House; passed by ≥2/3 of the total membership of that House.
3. Other House investigates or causes the charge to be investigated; President has right to appear and to be represented.
4. If the investigating House passes a resolution by ≥2/3 of its total membership declaring that the charge has been sustained, the President is removed from the date of that resolution.

Examination: ground (violation of the Constitution); either House may initiate; special notice and majorities; investigation by the other House; right to appear/representation.

sections.heading: Procedure steps
sections.body:
1. Charge preferred by either House (violation of the Constitution).
2. Notice: ≥14 days; signed by ≥1/4 of total membership.
3. Initiating House passes by ≥2/3 of total membership.
4. Other House investigates; President may appear and be represented.
5. Sustaining resolution by ≥2/3 of total membership of investigating House → removal from date of resolution.
